composition_label: Journey recommendations -> Ticket triage & routing -> Guided setup

construction.implementation_origin: New implementation written in the isolated build directory; no repository or other build content read or copied.

input_envelope.schema_version: Exactly integer 1; booleans are not integers for validation.

request.user: {id: string, goals: unique string array, completed: unique action-ID array}
request.actions: 1..200 objects {id, title, goals, prerequisites, weight}; ID and title are strings; goals and prerequisites are unique string arrays; weight is an integer 0..1000.
request.routing: {rules: ordered array of at most 100 rule objects, default: route object}
request.setup_events: Ordered array of unique action IDs to complete during this run.

shared_schema.rule_schema: All route fields plus keywords (1..50 unique strings) and source (ticket | journey | either).
shared_schema.output_envelope: The unchanged input envelope plus status=ok and stages={journey, triage, guided}. Partial internal envelopes have status=processing and only completed stages.

stage_outputs.journey: user_id, eligible_next_actions, two steps with action_id/score/matched_goals, second_step_condition
stage_outputs.triage: ticket_id, user_id, journey_action_ids, matched_rule (zero-based index or null), route
stage_outputs.guided: ticket_id, user_id, category, priority, journey_action_ids, steps (action_id/state/missing_prerequisites/owner/team), next_actions, progress (completed/total/percent), status

shared_schema.errors: {status: error, error: human-readable string}; stdout is one JSON object and CLI exits 2.
invariants: Unknown and missing object fields are rejected.
Strings must be nonblank and no longer than 2000 characters; ordinary string arrays contain at most 200 items.
Action IDs are unique; prerequisite references exist; the graph is acyclic.
Initially completed actions must include their complete prerequisite closure.
Each stage output is compared with canonical deterministic output before the next handoff; forged IDs, routing and progress are rejected.
Duplicate JSON object keys and non-finite JSON numbers are rejected by the CLI parser.
A request without two feasible unfinished actions is a validation error rather than a partial journey.

cross_stage_handoffs.data: Validated user ID and two selected action IDs; selected action titles and goal tags supply the journey text used by configurable routing rules.
Validated ticket/user IDs, journey action IDs, category, priority, accountable team/owner and route-specific setup actions.

behavior.journey: Rank actions by descending 1001 * exact shared goal count + configured weight, then lexicographic action ID. Select the first feasible pair in ranked order: first prerequisites must already be complete, second prerequisites must be complete after first. Return all currently eligible next actions.
behavior.triage: Case-insensitive substring keyword matching against configured ticket, selected journey, or combined context. The highest-priority matching rule wins; equal priorities use configuration order. Use the accountable default route if no rules match.
behavior.guided: Build the dependency closure of the recommended journey and routed setup actions. Topologically order the plan in lexicographic ready batches. Replay completion events in supplied order, rejecting incomplete prerequisites, outside-plan events or repeated completions. Report complete/ready/blocked steps and plan-local completion percentage rounded to two decimals.
behavior.progress_tracking: Initial completions plus validated request events determine progress. The full request and results are returned for the caller to persist; the CLI has no hidden state and does not write progress files.
behavior.determinism: No clock, randomness, external services or model calls affect results. Input is deep-copied and remains unchanged.
behavior.synthetic_fixture: Synthetic seller selects verify then list; payout ticket routes to synthetic payments support, adding billing/payout prerequisites. Completed register and verify yield 2/5 steps complete, or 40 percent.

included: Shared strict schema and semantic validation
Configurable deterministic support categorization and priority
Routed dependency-driven setup and event-based progress
Synthetic input fixture and standard-library unittest suite
JSON CLI success and file/validation error contracts
excluded: Live providers, LLM steps or injected model hooks
Production identity, payment or helpdesk integrations
Persistent database, authentication, authorization and multi-user state
Probabilistic language understanding and trained classifiers
Enterprise operations, retries, SLAs and deployment
Human notification delivery and external task execution

cli_example.stdout: One JSON object with status ok and all three validated stages.

coverage: Personalization, no-goal fallback and priority ties
Dependency closure, completion ordering and progress
Cyclic/unknown dependencies and incomplete initial closure
Unknown routed actions, outside-plan and duplicate completion events
Malformed shapes, boolean weights, blank owners and invalid priorities
Forged intermediate handoffs and final progress
CLI success, usage errors, missing files, malformed JSON, duplicate JSON keys, non-finite numbers and encoding errors
